root_cause.text: AppArmor’s rawdata files in `security/apparmor/apparmorfs.c` used a single `aa_loaddata` pointer in `inode->i_private` without an inode-level refcount, so profile removal could free the `struct aa_loaddata` via the profile’s last reference while `seq_rawdata_open()` or `rawdata_open()` was still dereferencing that dangling pointer.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE states “the rawdata inodes are not refcounted” and that during profile removal “the vfs and profile destruction race, resulting in the use after free”; the patch fixes this by adding separate `count` and `pcount` refs, changing opens to `aa_get_i_loaddata(inode->i_private)`, and making profile teardown drop `pcount` which later removes fs entries and only then drops the inode `count`.

intent_record.how: At runtime, this changes which reference-counted object cleanup routine is invoked when rawdata_f_data is freed, ensuring the associated i-loaddata object is released using the correct API instead of the generic loaddata release function.

intent_record.what: In the copy_from_user() failure path inside aa_simple_write_to_buffer(), the cleanup call changed from aa_put_loaddata(data) to aa_put_i_loaddata(data), and a comment was added noting that this path should trigger free without needing to put pcount.
intent_record.how: On user-copy failure, the function now uses a different teardown helper that frees the load data directly instead of performing the previous reference-counted put path, ensuring the allocated object is released in the intended way for this error case.

intent_record.what: In policy_update(), the call to aa_put_loaddata(data) was replaced with aa_put_profile_loaddata(data) after aa_replace_profiles(ns, label, mask, data), and a multi-line comment was added explaining that this operation drops the pcount and may free the load data if no profiles reference it.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the code now releases the load data using the profile-specific reference-counting helper rather than the generic one, ensuring the correct ownership accounting path is used after profile replacement and preventing mismatched reference handling or premature/leaked cleanup.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the profile-specific loaddata release helper in profile removal to correctly clean up loaded profile data.

intent_record.how: This changes which reference-release helper is used for the `data` object when removing profiles, ensuring the profile-specific load-data cleanup path is invoked rather than the generic loaddata release routine.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix seq_rawdata_open() to use the correct inode-specific loaddata reference helpers and matching cleanup path.
intent_record.what: In seq_rawdata_open(), the code now calls aa_get_i_loaddata() instead of __aa_get_loaddata() when retrieving loaddata from inode->i_private, and it now balances the reference with aa_put_i_loaddata() instead of aa_put_loaddata() on single_open() failure. The comment on the !data return path was removed.

At runtime, it preserves proper ownership handling when opening the seq file and ensures the reference is released with the matching inode-aware put helper if open setup fails.

intent_record.how: At runtime, the release path now decrements/releases a different load-data reference type, so the file teardown uses the interface-specific cleanup function instead of the generic one. This changes which ownership/accounting path is followed when the seq file is closed.

intent_record.what: In rawdata_open(), the code now calls aa_get_i_loaddata(inode->i_private) instead of __aa_get_loaddata(inode->i_private). The comment "lost race: this entry is being reaped" was removed from the subsequent NULL check, but the NULL check and -ENOENT return remain unchanged.

intent_record.what: In __aa_fs_create_rawdata(), after successfully creating the top-level directory entry and after each successful creation of the 'abi' and 'revision' files, the code now calls aa_get_i_loaddata(rawdata) before storing the returned dentry in rawdata->dents[].

intent_record.how: This increases the reference count or lifetime hold on the rawdata object whenever the hash dentry is created, preventing the associated load data from being released too early while the filesystem entry is still in use.

intent_record.what: In __aa_fs_create_rawdata(), the code now calls aa_get_i_loaddata(rawdata) after successfully creating each of the two rawdata files ('compressed_size' and 'raw_data'), and it adds a matching aa_put_i_loaddata(rawdata) in the fail path before returning an error. intent_record.intent_summary: Split loaddata lifetime management into separate filesystem and profile reference counts to correctly coordinate cleanup and raw policy data removal.
intent_record.what: The comment for `struct aa_loaddata` was rewritten and expanded with field-by-field documentation, and a new `struct kref pcount;` member was added immediately after the existing `count` field.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the struct now tracks two separate reference counts: one for inode/filesystem ownership and one for profile ownership. This enables delayed cleanup and filesystem entry removal to be tied to the profile refcount, while the existing count continues to protect dentries and inode opens. The updated comment clarifies the locking and lifetime rules for accessing loaddata entries in `ns->rawdata_list`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Split loaddata reference management into separate inode and profile reference counts to fix incorrect lifetime handling.
intent_record.what: The patch renames and splits the loaddata reference helpers: __aa_get_loaddata becomes aa_get_i_loaddata and now unconditionally increments data->count with kref_get() when data is non-NULL; aa_get_loaddata becomes aa_get_profile_loaddata and now increments a separate data->pcount. Similarly, aa_put_loaddata is renamed to aa_put_i_loaddata and still decrements data->count via aa_loaddata_kref, while a new aa_put_profile_loaddata is added to decrement data->pcount via a new aa_ploaddata_kref. A new aa_ploaddata_kref() prototype is also declared, and the comments are updated to describe the two distinct reference types.
intent_record.how: Runtime behavior now distinguishes between two independent reference-counting lifetimes for the same loaddata object: one for inode/internal references and one for profile references. This avoids the previous mixed use of a single counter and removes the conditional 'get unless zero' behavior for these helpers, meaning callers now take a normal reference on the appropriate counter as long as the pointer is non-NULL. It enables separate reclamation paths for the two ownership domains and prevents profile and internal references from interfering with each other's lifetime management.

intent_record.intent_summary: Separate loaddata filesystem removal from final object freeing by introducing distinct refcount callbacks and cleanup paths.
intent_record.what: The patch splits the old loaddata release path into two separate cleanup routines: it adds a new direct-free helper `do_loaddata_free()` plus a `aa_loaddata_kref()` callback that frees `hash`, `name`, `data`, and the struct itself; it renames the existing work handler from `do_loaddata_free()` to `do_ploaddata_rmfs()`, adds a comment before removing rawdata from fs, and changes the work callback `aa_ploaddata_kref()` to use `container_of(..., pcount)` instead of `count`, initialize the work item with `do_ploaddata_rmfs`, and schedule that work.
intent_record.how: Runtime cleanup is now split into two phases: dropping the last `pcount` schedules work to remove the rawdata filesystem reference under the namespace lock and then decrements the associated `icount`, while the separate `aa_loaddata_kref()` path now performs the actual memory release of the loaddata object. This changes ownership/lifetime handling so filesystem removal and object freeing are no longer performed in the same callback.

intent_record.intent_summary: Initialize the pcount reference counter when allocating aa_loaddata to prevent reference-counting bugs.

intent_record.how: This ensures the pcount reference counter in the allocated aa_loaddata structure starts in a valid initialized state, preventing use of an uninitialized kref if later code increments, decrements, or otherwise relies on pcount.

The old pattern was that profile files used a single `aa_loaddata` pointer via `inode->i_private` without inode-level refcounting, e.g. the previous code had `rawdata_open()` doing `file->private_data = aa_get_loaddata(profile->rawdata);` from a profile proxy and `rawdata_release()` freeing it, while profile removal could race with `seq_rawdata_open()`/`rawdata_open()`. The profile-side files were changed to symlinks (`securityfs_create_symlink("raw_sha1", ...)`, `securityfs_create_symlink("raw_abi", ...)`, `securityfs_create_symlink("raw_data", ...)`) instead of directly storing rawdata pointers in profile inodes, and rawdata removal is now coordinated under the namespace lock in `__aa_fs_remove_rawdata()` / `__aa_fs_list_remove_rawdata()`. This shows the fix is already present and the original dangling-pointer construct is absent.

    apparmor: move to per loaddata files, instead of replicating in profiles
    
    The loaddata sets cover more than just a single profile and should
    be tracked at the ns level. Move the load data files under the namespace
    and reference the files from the profiles via a symlink.
    
    Signed-off-by: John Johansen <john.johansen@canonical.com>
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is no longer present in this commit. The old pattern of using a single loaddata pointer from a profile/inode without an inode-level refcount has been replaced by namespace-tracked rawdata files and explicit loaddata refcounting. In this snippet, `rawdata_open()` now does `file->private_data = __aa_get_loaddata(inode->i_private);` and returns `-ENOENT` if the entry is being reaped, while `rawdata_release()` drops the reference with `aa_put_loaddata(file->private_data);`. The profile-side raw files are no longer direct files on `profile->proxy`; instead `__aa_fs_profile_mkdir()` creates symlinks like `securityfs_create_symlink("raw_data", dir, target, NULL);`, `securityfs_create_symlink("raw_sha1", ...)`, and `securityfs_create_symlink("raw_abi", ...)`, which avoids the dangling `inode->i_private`/profile lifetime issue. The commit also adds `__aa_fs_remove_rawdata()` and `__aa_fs_list_remove_rawdata()` to clean up namespace rawdata entries, further indicating the fix is already present.
